questions.stem: Two forces $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ act on a particle. The force $\mathbf{P}$ has magnitude 7 N and acts due north. The resultant of $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ is a force of magnitude 10 N acting in a direction with bearing $120°$. Find

parts.text:
(i) the magnitude of $\mathbf{Q}$,
(ii) the direction of $\mathbf{Q}$, giving your answer as a bearing.
(9)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathbf{R} = \frac{10\sqrt{3}}{2}\mathbf{i} - 5\mathbf{j}$ M1 A1
Using $\mathbf{P} = 7\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{R} - \mathbf{P}$ to obtain $\mathbf{Q} = 5\sqrt{3}\mathbf{i} - 12\mathbf{j}$ M1 A1
Magnitude $= \sqrt{[(5\sqrt{3})^2+12^2]} \approx 14.8\ \mathrm{N}$ (AWRT) M1 A1
angle with $\mathbf{i} = \arctan(12/5\sqrt{3}) \approx 64.2°$ M1 A1
bearing $\approx 144°$ (AWRT) A1
(9)
Alternative method
Vector triangle correct B1
$Q^2 = 10^2+7^2+2\times 10\times 7\cos 60$ M1 A1
$Q \approx 14.8\ \mathrm{N}$ (AWRT) A1
$\frac{14.8}{\sin 120} = \frac{10}{\sin\theta}$ M1 A1$\surd$
$\Rightarrow \theta = 35.8, \Rightarrow$ bearing 144 (AWRT) M1 A1, A1
(9)

questions.stem:
A parcel of weight 10 N lies on a rough plane inclined at an angle of $30°$ to the horizontal. A horizontal force of magnitude $P$ newtons acts on the parcel, as shown in Figure 2. The parcel is in equilibrium and on the point of slipping up the plane. The normal reaction of the plane on the parcel is 18 N. The coefficient of friction between the parcel and the plane is $\mu$.
Find

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) R(perp to plane): $P\sin 30 + 10\cos 30 = 18$ M1 A1
Solve: $P \approx 18.7\ \mathrm{N}$ M1 A1
(4)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) R(// to plane): $P\cos 30 = 10\sin 30 + F$ M1 A1
$F = 18\mu$ used M1
Sub and solve: $\mu = 0.621$ or $0.62$ M1 A1
(5)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The horizontal force is removed.
(c) Determine whether or not the parcel moves.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) Normal reaction now $= 10\cos 30$ M1 A1
Component of weight down plane $= 10\sin 30 (= 5\ \mathrm{N})$ (seen) B1
$F_{\max} = \mu R_{\mathrm{new}} \approx 5.37\ \mathrm{N}$ (AWRT 5.4) M1
$5.37 > 5 \Rightarrow$ does not slide A1 cso
(5)

questions.stem:
[In this question the horizontal unit vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are due east and due north respectively.]
A model boat $A$ moves on a lake with constant velocity $(-\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. At time $t=0$, $A$ is at the point with position vector $(2\mathbf{i}-10\mathbf{j})$ m. Find

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the direction in which $A$ is moving, giving your answer as a bearing.
(3)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
At time $t=0$, a second boat $B$ is at the point with position vector $(-26\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$ m.
Given that the velocity of $B$ is $(3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$,
(c) show that $A$ and $B$ will collide at a point $P$ and find the position vector of $P$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) P.v. of $A$ at time $t = (2-t)\mathbf{i}+(-10+6t)\mathbf{j}$
p.v. of $B$ at time $t = (-26+3t)\mathbf{i}+(4+4t)\mathbf{j}$ B1 (either)
(E.g.) $\mathbf{i}$ components equal $\Rightarrow 2-t = -26+3t \Rightarrow t=7$ M1 A1
$\mathbf{j}$ components at $t=7$: $A: -10+6t = 32$ M1
$B: 4+4t = 32$
Same, so collide at $t=7$ s at point with p.v. $(-5\mathbf{i}+32\mathbf{j})$ m A1 cso
(5)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Given instead that $B$ has speed 8 m s$^{-1}$ and moves in the direction of the vector $(3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$,
(d) find the distance of $B$ from $P$ when $t=7$ s.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) New velocity of $B = \frac{8}{5}(3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ B1
P.v. of $B$ at 7 s $= -26\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}+1.6(3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})\times 7 = 7.6\mathbf{i}+48.8\mathbf{j}$ M1 A1
$\overrightarrow{PB} = \mathbf{b}-\mathbf{p} = 12.6\mathbf{i}+16.8\mathbf{j}$ (in numbers) M1
Distance $= \sqrt{(12.6^2+16.8^2)} = 21\ \mathrm{m}$ M1 A1
(6)

questions.stem:
A fixed wedge has two plane faces, each inclined at $30°$ to the horizontal. Two particles $A$ and $B$, of mass $3m$ and $m$ respectively, are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string. Each particle moves on one of the plane faces of the wedge. The string passes over a smooth light pulley fixed at the top of the wedge. The face on which $A$ moves is smooth. The face on which $B$ moves is rough. The coefficient of friction between $B$ and this face is $\mu$. Particle $A$ is held at rest with the string taut. The string lies in the same vertical plane as lines of greatest slope on each plane face of the wedge, as shown in Figure 3.
The particles are released from rest and start to move. Particle $A$ moves downwards and particle $B$ moves upwards. The accelerations of $A$ and $B$ each have magnitude $\frac{1}{10}g$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) By considering the motion of $A$, find, in terms of $m$ and $g$, the tension in the string.
(3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) By considering the motion of $B$, find the value of $\mu$.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $F$: R(perp): $R = mg\cos 30$ M1 A1
R(//): $T - mg\sin 30 - F = m\cdot\frac{1}{10}g$ M1 A2, 1, 0
Using $F = \mu R$ M1
$\frac{6}{5}mg - \frac{1}{2}mg - \mu mg\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \frac{1}{10}mg$ M1
$\Rightarrow \mu = 0.693$ or $0.69$ or $\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}$ A1
(8)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the resultant force exerted by the string on the pulley, giving its magnitude and direction.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) Magn of force on pulley $= 2T\cos 60 = \frac{6}{5}mg$ M1 A1$\surd$
Direction is vertically downwards B1 (cso)
(3)

questions.question_text:
A fixed wedge has two plane faces, each inclined at $30°$ to the horizontal. Two particles $A$ and $B$, of mass $3m$ and $m$ respectively, are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string. Each particle moves on one of the plane faces of the wedge. The string passes over a smooth light pulley fixed at the top of the wedge. The face on which $A$ moves is smooth. The face on which $B$ moves is rough. The coefficient of friction between $B$ and this face is $\mu$. Particle $A$ is held at rest with the string taut. The string lies in the same vertical plane as lines of greatest slope on each plane face of the wedge, as shown in Figure 3.
The particles are released from rest and start to move. Particle $A$ moves downwards and particle $B$ moves upwards. The accelerations of $A$ and $B$ each have magnitude $\frac{1}{10}g$.
(a) By considering the motion of $A$, find, in terms of $m$ and $g$, the tension in the string.
(3)
(b) By considering the motion of $B$, find the value of $\mu$.
(8)
(c) Find the resultant force exerted by the string on the pulley, giving its magnitude and direction.
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $A$: $3mg\sin 30 - T = 3m\cdot\frac{1}{10}g$ M1 A1
$\Rightarrow T = \frac{6}{5}mg$ A1
(3)
(b) $F$: R(perp): $R = mg\cos 30$ M1 A1
R(//): $T - mg\sin 30 - F = m\cdot\frac{1}{10}g$ M1 A2, 1, 0
Using $F = \mu R$ M1
$\frac{6}{5}mg - \frac{1}{2}mg - \mu mg\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \frac{1}{10}mg$ M1
$\Rightarrow \mu = 0.693$ or $0.69$ or $\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}$ A1
(8)
(c) Magn of force on pulley $= 2T\cos 60 = \frac{6}{5}mg$ M1 A1$\surd$
Direction is vertically downwards B1 (cso)
(3)
